advisor_identified: Historian of modern Europe and France; associate professor of History and Geography at Morgan State University.

doctorate.title: The "exotic" Black African in the French social imagination in the 1920s.

evidence.says: Morgan State identifies Brett Berliner as an associate professor of History and Geography specializing in modern Europe and France, and lists a history PhD from the University of Massachusetts Amherst.
The UMass Amherst History Department lists Brett A. Berliner among its alumni with a PhD in 1999 and identifies his book Ambivalent Desire, also listed on his Morgan State faculty page.

The university repository records Brett A. Berliner as author of The "exotic" Black African in the French social imagination in the 1920s., dated 1999, with degree Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.), in the History Department Dissertations Collection.

In his 2001 article Dancing dangerously: colonizing the exotic at the Bal Negre in the inter-war years, Berliner cites his dissertation under the deposited title and identifies it as a University of Massachusetts Amherst PhD dissertation, 1999 (note 3, publicly indexed publisher text).

notes: The linked AHA record matches the advisor's name, history department, institution, year and dissertation subject. Its title begins "Mediating between Modernity and Savagery" and differs from the deposited title given above. The match is an identification inference supported by those agreements; the sources consulted do not explicitly document the title change.
